articles.title: Some Meta employees reportedly ‘scared’ of the company’s Muse AI Agent that AI head Alexandr Wang ‘champions’; fears include 'spying' and ...
articles.summary: Meta’s stock has seen a bump since the early-September debut of its AI agent Muse. The successful launch of the app, which has been No.
articles.body: Meta’s stock has seen a bump since the early-September debut of its AI agent Muse. The successful launch of the app, which has been No. 1 in Apple’s App Store for two weeks, has brought a new level of fame and acclaim to Meta’s AI lab head Alexandr Wang. Wang has succeeded in building hype for Muse, in part with an unconventional internet campaign. The young tech executive was handpicked by Mark Zuckerberg last year to oversee Meta’s AI efforts.However as Meta bets big on Muse AI agent, there are reportedly some warning signs. Meta employees testing the company’s Muse AI agent have reportedly warned that Muse AI agent appeared to access encrypted private messages and may have pulled details from other users’ conversations. According to a Reuters report, citing internal chats, the warnings echoed complaints from early users who said that Muse appeared to read their private messages and sometimes responded unpredictably.In one test, Muse offered to contact a seller about a coffee table pickup even though the employee had made no such request. The agent said it had “pulled in some context about a coffee table pickup that doesn’t seem to be yours.” The employee flagged the incident as a “possible cross-account context leak,” according to Reuters.A chat about fishing turns to bank balancesAnother employee was discussing fishing with Muse when the agent sent an unsolicited message listing what it described as balances of $2,722.58 at Capital One and $5,899.57 at Charles Schwab. It was unclear whether the figures came from real accounts. In a separate exchange, Muse sent an employee a definition of money laundering without being asked. “Got a random ping from Muse about something I definitely did not ask for,” the employee wrote.One employee told colleagues that Muse accidentally switched their dog to a premium insurance plan costing $888 a month, up from $200, Reuters reported. The employee said they were unable to recover the money.Incidentally, Meta started receiving privacy-related complaints from Muse users as early as September. An Inc Magazine reporter, Jason Aten, claimed that he was shocked when it became clear to him that Muse was digging through private messages on his Mac without permission. He claimed he not only "never gave it permission to read my messages. In fact, I remember explicitly choosing not to let it have access to my messages, calendar, and other personal information." Rather, the agent was syncing messages from a local database, which Aten said was activated without his knowledge. "Snooping through the private database of messages on my Mac doesn’t feel safe or private to me. Lying about it isn’t great either," he added.What Meta said on the Muse 'spying' claimsMeta’s spokesperson, Daniel Roberts, told Reuters that these were “isolated incidents,” and internally employees were told that “the agent appeared to be hallucinating messages in response to built-in prompts pushing it to engage with users in between sessions.” In those cases, an AI team member said the hallucinations were “unfortunately” biased “towards the most uncomfortable topics, like finances/security/safety, which sucks.”Speaking to Reuters, Roberts reiterated that “many of the messages flagged by employees as potential account mix-ups were hallucinations” that Meta had already addressed. However, he declined to respond to Reuters' questions on the prevalence or persistence of the issues the AI team member discussed.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? articles.title: GTA 6 is out, but this Bengaluru’s flyover isn’t: City's ‘Stonehenge’, 9 years in the making, misses another deadline
articles.summary: BENGALURU: Bengaluru's much-delayed Ejipura flyover, dubbed the city's 'Stonehenge' for its years of stalled construction and unfinished pillars, is
articles.body: BENGALURU: Bengaluru's much-delayed Ejipura flyover, dubbed the city's 'Stonehenge' for its years of stalled construction and unfinished pillars, is staring at yet another deadline miss.Nearly nine years after work began, the 2.5km elevated corridor may not be ready even by December-end, prolonging commuters' wait for relief along the busy Koramangala–Ejipura–Madiwala stretch.Originally scheduled for completion in November 2019, the project has endured repeated deadline extensions, contractor failure, failed tenders, land acquisition hurdles, delayed clearances and disputes over payments.Despite a change of contractor and several assurances from civic authorities, the flyover remains unfinished.From 2017 to 2022: Simplex fails to complete the projectThe flyover was originally awarded to Kolkata-based Simplex Infrastructure Ltd in 2017, with an estimated project cost of Rs 158 crore. BBMP issued the work order on May 4, 2017, and the project was scheduled for completion by November 2019.However, construction faced problems from the beginning. Delays in traffic police clearances, permission for controlled blasting and land acquisition affected the pace of work.By 2020, BBMP was still struggling to acquire portions of land required for the flyover, including property belonging to St John's Hospital, the Central Public Works Department and the Indian Institute of Astrophysics.The Covid-19 pandemic further affected labour mobilisation in 2020.Despite repeated deadline extensions, Simplex failed to complete the project. The company was facing financial difficulties, and construction eventually ground to a halt.A public interest litigation filed in 2021 brought the matter before the Karnataka high court. Following judicial intervention, BBMP terminated Simplex's contract in March 2022.By then, the civic body had spent around Rs 75 crore on the project. It also forfeited the contractor's security deposit of Rs 10.16 crore and imposed a penalty of around Rs 2.5 crore.Three failed tenders before BSCPL took overFinding a replacement contractor proved equally difficult.BBMP floated a fresh tender in August 2022, but the process was recalled. Another tender, floated in January 2023 for Rs 144 crore, attracted only one bidder, Hyderabad-based BSCPL Infrastructure Ltd, which quoted around Rs 205 crore, approximately 44% above the estimated amount.The bid did not receive financial approval, forcing BBMP to cancel the tender in February 2023.After revising the estimates and introducing a price-adjustment clause, BBMP eventually awarded the remaining work to BSCPL Infrastructure Ltd in November 2023, with a 15-month completion deadline.The cost of completing the remaining construction was pegged at Rs 176.1 crore, excluding GST.However, the change in contractor did not immediately accelerate the project.BSCPL flagged delays in land acquisition, mobilisation payments and access to the casting yard. The company also had to obtain an Indian Institute of Science (IISc) assessment of the structure built by Simplex before proceeding with further construction.The assessment was completed in May 2024, several months after the new contractor took over.BBMP also issued notices to BSCPL over slow progress and imposed a penalty of Rs 25 lakh.Land acquisition, trees and ramps become fresh hurdlesEven as construction picked up in 2025, land acquisition near St John's Medical College Hospital continued to affect the construction of ramps.The project also faced objections from residents over BBMP's proposal to remove 157 trees along Koramangala's 100 Feet Road. More than 150 objections and suggestions were received before the deadline for public submissions in January 2025.Residents suggested changes to the ramp design and alignment to save trees, while activists questioned the changing number of trees proposed for removal.In January 2026, GBA chief commissioner M Maheshwar Rao directed officials to mark the land required at St John's Hospital and begin construction of five portal piers. Hospital management agreed to allow temporary use of a portion of its land along the compound wall.Officials were directed to install barricades and rebuild the compound wall after construction.The administration subsequently announced fresh completion targets, but the project continued to miss them.Why December-end is also looking difficultThe project has already seen its completion targets move from November 2019 to 2020, December 2021, 2025 and multiple dates in 2026.The main elevated corridor still has pending construction and finishing work, including ramps, pavement, crash barriers, drainage, lighting, lane markings and road signage.The additional entry and exit ramps towards Sarjapur Road also require further land acquisition and may take longer to complete.For commuters, the concern is no longer just when the flyover will be inaugurated, but whether the entire project will finally be completed after years of disruption."GTA 6 is getting released yet Ejipura flyover couldn't get be operational yet," a social media user posted, summing up the frustration surrounding the project.What is the GTA 6 hype about?The comparison is particularly relevant as Grand Theft Auto VI (GTA 6), one of the most anticipated video games in history, has finally rolled out worldwide after a 13-year wait. The latest instalment in Rockstar Games' hugely popular franchise was released on November 19, with players across countries gaining access at midnight local time.The previous instalment, GTA V, was released in 2013 and went on to become one of the best-selling video games ever. The Grand Theft Auto franchise has sold more than 470 million units worldwide, with GTA V alone accounting for over 230 million.The new game takes players to Leonida, Rockstar's fictional version of Florida, with Vice City, inspired by Miami, at its centre. Its story follows Lucia Caminos and Jason Duval, a couple drawn deeper into the criminal underworld as they attempt to improve their lives.The anticipation surrounding the release has been enormous. Take-Two Interactive, Rockstar's parent company, saw its shares rise more than 8% on the eve of the launch. Internet provider Chorus in New Zealand also prepared for around 35 petabytes of additional network traffic as players began downloading the game.For GTA fans, the 13-year wait has finally ended. For Bengalureans waiting for the Ejipura flyover, however, the countdown continues.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Bengaluru | Silver Rate in Bengaluru | Bank Holidays in Bengaluru | Public Holidays in Bengaluru | Bengaluru AQI | Weather in Bengaluru | Petrol Price in Bengaluru | Diesel Price in Bengaluru | CNG Price in Bengaluru | LPG Price in BengaluruStay updated with the latest Bengaluru news. articles.title: 'Must uphold open regionalism': Xi calls for free trade & stronger Asia-Pacific cooperation at APEC
articles.summary: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for free and open trade, stronger regional cooperation and improved economic connectivity across the
articles.body: Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday called for free and open trade, stronger regional cooperation and improved economic connectivity across the Asia-Pacific region, as leaders gathered for the 33rd Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen.Addressing the summit, Xi urged member economies to uphold open regionalism, strengthen economic cooperation and remove barriers that restrict trade and growth. His remarks come amid continuing trade tensions between the United States and China and growing geopolitical divisions over technology, security and global supply chains.Xi called for efforts to "unblock economic channels" and create more opportunities for growth across the Asia-Pacific region. He also advocated smart customs systems and better regional data governance to facilitate trade and improve economic connectivity.The Chinese president stressed the need to build an open and inclusive framework for regional cooperation rather than arrangements that exclude certain economies."We must uphold open regionalism, steadily promote economy, build open but not exclusive cooperation," Xi said, according to Reuters.His remarks also focused on the importance of free and open trade at a time when protectionist policies, tariffs and restrictions on critical technologies are reshaping global commerce.Trump, Xi and Putin meeting amid geopolitical tensionsXi's address comes as US President Donald Trump, Russian President Vladimir Putin and the Chinese leader prepare for a high-profile trilateral meeting on the sidelines of the APEC summit.The discussions are expected to cover nuclear arms control, the wars in Ukraine and Iran, trade disputes and competition over artificial intelligence.Trump has presented the meeting as an opportunity to negotiate with two of Washington's major geopolitical rivals and explore ways to address international conflicts.The trilateral engagement is particularly important following the expiration of the New START nuclear arms control treaty between Washington and Moscow in February 2026. Trump has expressed interest in negotiating a new agreement that would also include China.However, expectations of an immediate breakthrough remain limited, given differences in the countries' nuclear capabilities and strategic priorities.US-China trade tensions remain a challengeDespite diplomatic engagement between Trump and Xi, economic tensions between the world's two largest economies remain unresolved.The trade truce reached last year following reciprocal tariff increases is due to expire on January 10 next year. Washington has also accused Beijing of not fully honouring commitments to increase purchases of American agricultural products and ease restrictions on rare earth mineral exports.Competition over artificial intelligence and access to advanced semiconductors has added another dimension to the rivalry.Xi's call for open trade and regional economic cooperation therefore comes at a time when the Asia-Pacific region faces competing pressures from geopolitical rivalries, trade restrictions and disruptions to global supply chains.The APEC summit provides Beijing an opportunity to project itself as a supporter of regional economic integration while positioning China as a central player in shaping the future of Asia-Pacific cooperation.You use AI every day. articles.title: Pakistan minister who warned India over Indus Waters Treaty to attend SCO meet in Delhi
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: More than a year after India-Pakistan ties plunged following the Pahalgam terror attack, Pakistan's climate minister Musadik Malik is set to
articles.body: NEW DELHI: More than a year after India-Pakistan ties plunged following the Pahalgam terror attack, Pakistan's climate minister Musadik Malik is set to visit New Delhi to attend a Shanghai Cooperation Organisation (SCO) meeting.The visit will be the first by a Pakistani minister to India since May 2023.Malik will lead the Pakistani delegation at the SCO Civilisational Dialogue, scheduled to be held from November 20 to 22.The visit is significant as Malik was among the Pakistani leaders who issued sharp warnings against India's decision to place the long-standing Indus Waters Treaty (IWT) in abeyance following the Pakistan-sponsored Pahalgam terror attack.Reacting to India's move, Malik had warned that Pakistan would retaliate if its water supply was disrupted. "It has already been declared that whoever touches our water, their hands would be cut off," he had said."Pakistan's federal minister for climate change and environmental coordination, Musadik Masood Malik, will lead the Pakistan delegation to the first SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum, to be held in New Delhi, from 20-22 November 2026. Pakistan delegation will also participate in thematic sessions of the Forum and engage with SCO member States on the sidelines of the Forum," Pakistan foreign ministry said.According to Pakistan's Express Tribune, Malik's visit will be the first by a Pakistani minister to India since May 2023, when then foreign minister Bilawal Bhutto Zardari travelled to Goa to attend the SCO Council of foreign ministers meeting.It will also be the first such visit since India's counterterror military action against Pakistan under Operation Sindoor.The ministry of external affairs spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal had earlier confirmed that India had invited several countries, including all SCO member states, to the event and said New Delhi looked forward to hosting the dialogue.Proposed by India, the initiative seeks to promote cultural exchange, mutual understanding and people-to-people ties across the Eurasian region.Defence minister Rajnath Singh had announced India's plan to host the first SCO Civilisations Dialogue Forum at the SCO Council of Heads of Government meeting in Dushanbe, Tajikistan, on October 20.The SCO has 10 member states, including India, Pakistan, China and Russia. India became a full member of the grouping in 2017.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Wassily Kandinsky's painting Betonte Ecken sold for $85.8 million at a November 17 New York auction, almost doubling the artist's previous $44.8 million record as Christie's evening sale brought in $627 million
articles.summary: Wassily Kandinsky’s Betonte Ecken sold for $85.8 million at Christie’s New York on November 17, nearly doubling the artist’s previous auction record of
articles.body: Wassily Kandinsky’s Betonte Ecken sold for $85.8 million at Christie’s New York on November 17, nearly doubling the artist’s previous auction record of $44.8 million. The result came during a strong 20th Century Evening Sale that brought in $627 million, according to Christie’s press release.The Kandinsky was the top lot of the night, drawing intense bidding from clients on the phones and in the saleroom. Its sale set a new benchmark for the Russian abstract artist and helped define a market evening marked by competitive bidding across Impressionist, modern, and Latin American art. Read more about it, as per the release, here:A record for KandinskyBetonte Ecken was the clear centrepiece of the sale. After an intense bidding contest involving multiple clients, the painting sold for $85.8 million, far above Kandinsky’s previous record of $44.8 million.The result nearly doubled the artist’s prior high, a significant jump for a modern master whose market had already reached the tens of millions. Christie’s described the painting as a masterpiece and said the bidding reflected the depth of demand at the masterpiece level.The sale places Kandinsky among the artists whose work has crossed the $80 million threshold at auction. It also gives the artist a new benchmark that will shape expectations for future offerings of comparable quality.Christie’s $627 million nightChristie’s 20th Century Evening Sale totaled $626,621,400, selling 92 percent by lot and 95 percent by value. The auction included more than 70 lots spanning 500 years of art history. The sale featured strong bidding from Asia and from clients participating by phone and online. Christie’s said the results reflected an energetic market with passionate competition across categories.With this single evening, Christie’s year to date total for 20th and 21st Century Art in the Americas has already surpassed the category’s full year 2025 total. The result came on the first night of Christie’s 20/21 Fall Marquee Week.Other major resultsGustav Klimt’s Litzlbergkeller sold for $82.3 million to a client on the phone after nearly six minutes of competitive bidding. The result made it one of the strongest lots of the evening, just behind the Kandinsky.Pablo Picasso’s Le Baiser from the Heroes & Lovers collection sold for $31.2 million. A 1949 bronze by Alberto Giacometti from the collection of Herbert Lust sold for $26 million, with no reserve.Claude Monet also performed well. A luminous 1890 landscape from the collection of William I. Koch sold for $25.9 million, while a scene from 1875 brought $12.8 million, both above their high estimates.Records across categoriesThe sale produced six records. Kandinsky’s Betonte Ecken set a new artist record, while Cornelius Cornelisz van Haarlem’s Hercules and Achelous sold for $13.9 million.Wifredo Lam’s Ogue Orisa sold for $11.6 million, setting a new record for the artist. Fernando Botero’s monumental Horse sold for $5.2 million, also a new artist record.Hans Bellmer’s Jointure de boules (La Poupée) sold for $1.6 million, and Joan Miró’s Femme, monument sold for $11.8 million, setting a record for a Miró bronze. These results show that demand was not limited to a single artist or category.Collections that stood outSeveral single owner collections performed strongly. The Heroes & Lovers collection brought in $104.7 million, while the William I. Koch collection totaled $66.3 million.The Herbert Lust collection realized $42 million, and the Clive Davis collection brought $32.6 million. These results show that provenance and collection quality can add momentum to a sale.Christie’s co-heads of the 20th Century Evening Sale, Rachael White Young and Paige Kestenman, said the outcome reflected the vibrancy of the market. They noted that the sale followed a 10 day exhibition and drew eager bidding from start to finish.What the result meansThe Kandinsky record is the headline, but the broader message is that the market for major modern and Impressionist works remains active. Buyers were willing to compete for quality across a range of artists and categories.The $627 million total also shows that Christie’s was able to assemble a sale with enough depth to sustain interest beyond a single lot. The evening included works by Klimt, Picasso, Monet, Giacometti, Miró, and others, giving collectors multiple reasons to participate.For Kandinsky, the result changes the conversation around his market. For Christie’s, it sets a strong opening for Marquee Week and signals that the demand for major works is still there.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.body: KOLKATA: Trinamool Congress (TMC) MP Mahua Moitra has alleged that her convoy was attacked by a mob carrying BJP flags on Thursday, accusing police personnel present at the scene of failing to intervene.In a video recorded on her phone and shared on social media platform X, Moitra claimed that the attack continued for over half an hour despite police presence. She also alleged that members of the mob physically lifted her car and moved it."I have been attacked today. This is my car. I have been attacked by the mob with police waiting, with police waiting who have done nothing. I have been attacked by the mob. My car has been physically lifted up and taken. And I have been attacked by the BJP with the same BJP guy—I recognise this face—by the same BJP guys with flags, with everything," she said.Moitra further accused the police of trying to remove her from the spot rather than taking action against those allegedly involved in the attack.She also questioned the Supreme Court and the Calcutta High Court over their response to the incident, referring to the contempt proceedings and addressing Solicitor General Tushar Mehta and Justice Dipankar Datta."You asked me to face eggs; look again, my car has been attacked. What have you done, Calcutta High Court?" she said.In another video, which showed a large crowd appearing to obstruct her car and throw eggs at the convoy, Moitra alleged that the police had failed to prevent the disruption despite receiving prior information about the programme."In spite of giving the police all information, they have allowed this BJP mob to come and disrupt the program and attack my convoy, which has police protection," she wrote on X.Calling herself one of the 78 women members of the Lok Sabha, the TMC MP also criticised the authorities over what she described as their failure to protect her."This is the voice of one of 78 women in the Lok Sabha. articles.title: A $3 million Australian home had no direct road access except through a shared driveway; a neighbour's wall and fence blocked its only access, leading to a $147,713 legal-cost dispute
articles.summary: A property worth around $3 million in Australia became the centre of a bitter neighbourhood dispute after its access to the road was obstructed by a
articles.body: A property worth around $3 million in Australia became the centre of a bitter neighbourhood dispute after its access to the road was obstructed by a neighbour's wall and fence. The disagreement over a shared driveway developed into an expensive legal battle, raising questions about how far property owners can go when exercising their rights over adjoining land. What began as a problem involving access to a home eventually resulted in a dispute over legal costs totalling $147,713.The $3 million Australian home and the blocked shared drivewayThe property belonged to Catherine Coneliano, whose home is located on Fowler Road in Illawong, in southern Sydney. According to the ‘news’ (Australia), the house had no direct access to a public road. Its residents depended on a narrow shared driveway, which provided the only route for vehicles to enter and leave the property.The driveway was legally recognised as a right of way, meaning the owners had an established entitlement to use the adjoining land for access. However, that arrangement became a source of conflict after neighbouring property owners Emmanuel and Olivera Garcia carried out construction work along the boundary between the two properties.The dispute was not simply about the appearance of a fence or the placement of a wall. The changes affected the practical use of a route that the Conelianos needed to reach their home. With no alternative public-road entrance, even a relatively small obstruction could create significant difficulties for the household.According to the report by ‘news,’ the dispute eventually reached the NSW Land and Environment Court after attempts to resolve the matter through legal correspondence failed.The neighbour's wall and fence affected the accessThe disagreement centred on a concrete retaining wall and a metal fence constructed by the Garcias. Parts of these structures extended into the shared driveway, reducing the available space along an already narrow access route.Court documents described the effect of the construction as making it very difficult for Coneliano's vehicles to enter and leave the property. The problem was particularly important because the driveway was not an optional convenience. It was the only vehicle access connecting her home to the public road.Coneliano also raised concerns about other obstructions. According to the ‘news,’ she alleged that the neighbours regularly left parked cars, rubbish and other belongings in the driveway, making passage even more difficult.The combination of the structures and the alleged obstruction by vehicles and other items turned an everyday journey into a recurring problem.Legal letters failed to resolve the disagreementBefore starting court proceedings, Coneliano attempted to address the problem through her lawyers. Several letters were reportedly sent to the Garcias over a period of months, asking them to remove the sections of the wall and fence obstructing the driveway and to stop leaving vehicles and other items in the passage.However, the requests did not produce the desired outcome. The neighbours largely ignored the correspondence. When Coneliano's lawyers visited the right of way, they were reportedly asked by the Garcias to leave. Coneliano eventually commenced proceedings in the NSW Land and Environment Court.The case did not proceed to a full trial on the underlying driveway dispute. Instead, the parties attended mediation and reached an agreement before the matter could be fully heard.Under the agreement, the Garcias accepted that the obstructing sections of the retaining wall and metal fence would be removed. They also agreed to stop parking vehicles or leaving other items in the shared driveway. But this did not settle the financial consequences of the legal battle.The court considered who should pay the legal costsOnce the neighbours had reached an agreement through mediation, the remaining issue before Justice Richard Beasley was the payment of Coneliano's legal expenses.Coneliano asked the court to make the Garcias responsible for $147,713 in legal costs. The neighbours opposed the request, arguing that they had not been given a proper opportunity to resolve the dispute and that each side should pay its own legal expenses.However, the judge did not accept their position. As reported by the ‘news,’ Justice Beasley described Coneliano as the clear winner of the dispute, considering that she had achieved the outcome she had originally sought.The judge also found that the Garcias had largely ignored the concerns raised by their neighbour. Their failure to address the obstruction meant that Coneliano had been left with no alternative but to begin legal proceedings to secure access to her property.Although the judge supported her claim for legal costs, he did not immediately order payment of the precise $147,713 requested. Instead, he directed that the costs be agreed between the parties or assessed through the appropriate process.Australian property law places limits on interference with access rightsAccording to Whiteacre Legal, the owner of the property carrying the easement can generally install fences to secure the boundary, provided that sufficient access remains available for the reasonable use of the right of way.In Trewin v Felton, the court recognised that a property owner could install fencing along a right of way, provided reasonable access was maintained through suitable gates.Another decision, Dudley v Ainsworth, involved a fence that restricted access for larger vehicles and machinery. In Castle v Achdjian, a fence that completely blocked a right of way was also found to constitute substantial interference. The court ordered its removal.You use AI every day. articles.title: A Manhattan townhouse just 12½ feet wide has hit the market for $3.495 million; its unusual address, 322½ East 50th Street, traces back to a narrow lot carved out of a larger property more than a century ago
articles.summary: The skinny Manhattan townhouse at 322½ East 50th Street in Turtle Bay has hit the market with an asking price of $3.495 million.
articles.body: The skinny Manhattan townhouse at 322½ East 50th Street in Turtle Bay has hit the market with an asking price of $3.495 million. Measuring 12½ feet wide, the townhouse spans 3,118 square feet, with four bedrooms and 3½ bathrooms, according to the listing on StreetEasy. Wondering what the half in the address is? Well, it is certainly not a mistake. “Fractional addresses often are given to back-buildings that are constructed at the rear of a lot, behind the building that fronts directly onto the street,” architectural historian Andrew Alpern told the New York Post. “But they also show up sometimes where a standard lot is cut in half.” He says that is what happened here.How a 12½-foot strip of land became 322½Alpern believes the split happened around 1880 or 1885. At that time, one builder owned two adjoining lots that together were 50 feet wide. The builder appears to have joined one full lot with half of the other. That created a 37½-foot parcel for a tenement building. The leftover strip was 12½ feet wide. The strip became Lot 43½. As the neighbouring building was already numbered 322, the narrow house took the number 322½. The historian also shared a 1912 land book, which shows the old lot layout. Interestingly, the half symbol appears in both the street address and the lot number. It is a fun detail, Alpern adds. He also said each fractional address usually has its own reason for existing.Manhattan has several of these addresses. Another well-known example is the Millay House at 75½ Bedford Street in the West Village. It is 9½ feet wide. Its story is different, though. That lot began as a carriage entryway.Famous former residentsBeyond its unique name, this Manhattan townhouse also has a list of famous former owners. Huntington Hartford II, heir to the A&P supermarket fortune, once owned the property. Later, celebrity hairdresser Kenneth Battelle lived and worked there. Yes, the same person behind Jacqueline Kennedy’s bouffant hairstyle! Some of his famous clients included Marilyn Monroe, Audrey Hepburn and Judy Garland. He turned the top floor into a spa and wired the house with 125 telephone lines, according to the listing.Inside the houseThe beautiful townhouse, with four bedrooms and 3½ bathrooms, is located on a quiet residential block, just around the corner from Greenacre Park, known for its 25-foot waterfall. The listing says the townhouse has the kind of character that’s “nearly impossible to find in Midtown”. The parlour floor has tall windows with grapevine-patterned wrought iron. “Up the front steps, the parlour floor opens to a generous living room with a curved wall and recessed lighting, big enough for a grand piano. In back, the sitting room has tall ceilings, hardwood floors, and large south-facing windows framed in floral and grapevine ironwork. Crown moulding and period details carry throughout, and a white mantel with a dark stone surround and mirrored overmantel anchors the room,” the listing describes.The house also has wood-burning fireplaces and a skylit staircase that brings daylight to the top floor. The garden level has a curved-glass sunroom. It opens onto a private garden with stone paving, raised brick planters and mature trees. The townhouse also comes with a cellar containing about 605 square feet of unfinished space. It also has a washer-dryer hookup already in place.Dexter Guerrieri, president of Vandenberg, the brokerage handling the sale, told The Post that the asking price and relatively modest property taxes are the selling points. The house is also close to Greenacre Park and a short walk from the East River and Rockefeller Center, according to the listing.Ready to Make a Smarter Property Decision? articles.title: A 57-year-old Haryana woman is set to become teacher just 5 months before retirement, after 27-year legal battle over appointment letter she never received despite being asked to join govt school; HC ordered her appointment with benefits from 1999
articles.summary: CHANDIGARH: At 57, with just five months left before retirement, Jai Mala is finally set to walk into a classroom as a Sanskrit teacher, 27 years after
articles.body: CHANDIGARH: At 57, with just five months left before retirement, Jai Mala is finally set to walk into a classroom as a Sanskrit teacher, 27 years after she was asked to join a Haryana government school but never received her appointment letter.The Punjab and Haryana high court on Monday directed the Haryana government to appoint her with effect from June 10, 1999, along with all consequential benefits, setting aside the judgments of two lower courts that had rejected her claim.“Though I have only five months of service left before my scheduled retirement in April, I can’t wait to step into a classroom. This is what I have been waiting for,” Jai Mala, now 57, told TOI on Wednesday.The 27-year-long fight, however, came at a heavy personal cost. Her husband, Roop Chand, said the prolonged uncertainty and repeated disappointments took a toll on her mental and physical health. She slipped into depression and also suffered a cardiac attack, he said.“We spent lakhs of rupees, suffered disappointments, but I am happy that after 27 years of struggle, justice has prevailed,” Jai Mala said.Her ordeal began in December 1998, when she was called for an interview for the post of Sanskrit teacher. In June 1999, the district education officer scrutinised her certificates and asked her to join a government school in Rewari. However, the formal appointment letter never arrived.Despite approaching the authorities repeatedly, she failed to get the letter. She eventually filed a suit seeking appointment with effect from June 10, 1999, along with arrears of salary and allowances and interest.The Haryana government opposed her claim, arguing that she had not submitted a certificate establishing knowledge of Hindi up to the matriculation standard, a prerequisite for the post. It also disputed her contention that she had studied Hindi during her BA.The dispute centred on her educational qualifications. Jai Mala held BA and B.Ed degrees, with Sanskrit and English as subjects. She had also studied Hindi in both Part-I and Part-II of her BA.A trial court dismissed her suit on May 18, 2006. The Rewari district judge upheld the decision on October 11, 2006, forcing her to approach the high court.Before the high court, her counsel argued that the lower courts had overlooked documentary evidence showing that she had secured 106 out of 200 marks in Hindi in BA Part-I and 89 out of 200 in Part-II. Having passed Hindi at the graduation level, she possessed a qualification higher than the minimum knowledge of Hindi prescribed for the post, the counsel submitted.The state counsel maintained that the earlier judgments were based on a proper appreciation of the facts.The high court, however, found merit in Jai Mala's argument. Justice Manuja observed that the documentary evidence clearly established that she had studied Hindi during her BA.Referring to Haryana government's instructions dated June 16, 1979, and a Supreme Court judgment, the court held that a higher academic qualification in the prescribed subject could not be disregarded merely because she had not studied Hindi at the matriculation level.“Once the appellant-plaintiff acquired higher academic qualification in the very subject for which knowledge was prescribed, the mere fact that she had not studied Hindi at the matriculation level could not, by itself, have rendered her ineligible for the post,” Justice Manuja observed.The court also took note of the authorities asking her to join the school before withholding the formal appointment order.“The respondents’ conduct in asking the appellant to join and thereafter withholding the formal appointment order lends support to her case, reflecting a lack of due diligence on their part,” the bench said.With the high court ruling in her favour, Jai Mala said she was looking forward to starting work and performing her duties diligently.Her husband, who works as a computer teacher at a government college in Rewari, said their education helped them sustain the prolonged legal battle.“We could persist with this legal battle only because we are educated and understood the legal process. articles.title: Landsat images show Utah’s Cottonwood Fire turning green mountain terrain into a burn scar; by July 7, it had burned about 150 square miles
articles.summary: The Cottonwood Fire in Utah has rapidly burned about 150 square miles of land, turning lush green mountains into a significant burn scar, as shown in latest satellite imagery. Discover the impact of climate change, fire containment efforts, and the vital role of forest management.
articles.body: Two satellite images taken 24 days apart tell a worrying story. According to NASA's Earth Observatory, Landsat 8 and Landsat 9 satellites took images of the same section of Utah on 5 June and 29 June 2026. In these false-colour images, unburned vegetation appears bright green. The first image is of mountains that hadn’t been burned yet. The second shows a large brown scar across most of the picture. By 7 July, the Cottonwood Fire had burned about 150 square miles (390 square kilometres). NASA describes it as having been among the largest and most destructive fires in Utah and the nation up to that point in 2026.A dry season and a risky forecast The land was ready to burn. NASA notes that the winter saw below-average snowpack, while the start of summer was unusually warm and dry. The National Interagency Fire Center had warned that the Great Basin region and portions of the Rocky Mountains faced an increased threat of wildfire in July. On 7 July, firefighters were fighting nearly three dozen large early-season fires in the Western US. Among those, Utah stood out with 558 square miles burned across all its fires. Nationwide, the fires had already burned 5,265 square miles of territory. That's 46% more than the 10-year average for that point in the season. In terms of size, the Cottonwood Fire fell just shy of the Babylon Fire of eastern Utah.How fast the fire grewThe Cottonwood Fire grew very fast as well. NASA's Fire Events Data Suite uses three satellites with heat-detecting sensors. It showed the fire spreading north, east, and south, tripling in size over 12 hours on 23 June. On 26 June, it made another run to the north. University of Maryland scientist Tempest McCabe, who helped develop the tool, says it delivers consistent, easily accessible data that doesn't need to be specifically requested. That helps it often spot the start of a fire sooner than other sources. On 7 July, the fire was 56% contained with 1,289 firefighters on the ground. Forecasters expected hot, dry weather to continue.What burned and what survivedAmong the vegetation destroyed by the fire are ponderosa pine, oak, sagebrush and grass. Officials with the state's forestry division told news media that the fire had destroyed about 150 buildings. The Eagle Point Ski Resort lost over 100 condos and 30 cabins, and it reported damage to four out of the five chairlifts. However, some patches of green managed to survive, like the forests near the Tushar Campground, which hosts a 4-H summer camp. Beaver County officials credited forest work like clearing the brush and trimming branches with helping save the campground and nearby forests.Research supports the general idea. A 2026 Science paper titled ‘Wildfire damages and the cost-effective role of forest fuel treatments’ by Frederik Strabo, Calvin Bryan and Matthew Reimer studied 285 large wildfires across 11 Western States between 2017 and 2023. Each of those fires burned into at least US Forest Service fuel treatment. The team estimated that treatments like thinning and prescribed burns cut the total area burned by 36% compared with what would have burned without them. For every dollar spent, the expected benefits were about $3.73. While the study doesn't look at the Cottonwood Fire, it shows why preparation is important.Where climate comes into play Climate adds another layer. In a 2016 study published in the Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, John Abatzoglou and A. Park Williams found that human-caused climate change drove about 55% of the increase in fuel dryness from 1979 to 2015. By their estimates, climate change added about 4.2 million hectares of burned forest between 1984 and 2015, nearly doubling the total that would have been expected without it. Abatzoglou and Williams also say natural climate fluctuations play a role. The study looked at western forests as a whole and predated the fire, so it doesn't address the Cottonwood Fire.The Cottonwood Fire shows how quickly a green landscape can change. Satellites now help scientists and firefighters track fires in real time, which can help crews plan their response. Research also shows that taking care of forests before the fire begins can lessen the damage. Hot and dry conditions can raise the risk, and early preparation can really make a difference in saving a forest.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Gurgaon family cancels Jaipur destination wedding after groom’s father’s factory fire kills 14, resort refuses to refund Rs 16 lakh, consumer commission orders it to return Rs 16 lakh with interest and Rs 2.05 lakh compensation and costs
articles.summary: GURGAON: A Gurgaon family’s decision to cancel a destination wedding at a Jaipur resort after a fire at the groom’s father’s factory killed 14 workers has
articles.body: GURGAON: A Gurgaon family’s decision to cancel a destination wedding at a Jaipur resort after a fire at the groom’s father’s factory killed 14 workers has resulted in a consumer commission directing the resort to refund Rs 16 lakh, with 9% annual interest, besides paying Rs 1.5 lakh as compensation for mental harassment and Rs 55,000 towards litigation expenses.The District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission, Gurgaon, held The Rajasthali Resort & Spa, Jaipur, guilty of deficiency in service after it failed to refund the amount deposited by Gagan Bansal despite his requests to cancel the wedding functions following the tragedy.In its order, the commission directed the resort to refund the entire Rs 16 lakh along with interest at 9% per annum calculated from the dates of individual payments until realisation. It also directed the resort to pay the awarded amounts within 45 days of the order.According to the complaint, Bansal had booked the resort for his destination wedding after being attracted by offers of discounts and other facilities. He initially paid Rs 1 lakh in cash as booking money, followed by four RTGS transactions of Rs 4 lakh, Rs 5 lakh, Rs 4 lakh and Rs 2 lakh, taking the total payment to Rs 16 lakh.The dispute allegedly began when the resort sent him a draft contract after receiving the payments. Bansal told the commission that the draft contained increased rates and additional items in the paid list, contrary to the terms discussed during negotiations. Despite his objections, the resort allegedly insisted on the revised terms.The situation took a turn after a fire broke out at the groom’s father’s factory on May 28, 2024, engulfing 14 workers. The bride’s cousin was among those killed, while her uncle sustained injuries, the complaint stated.Bansal informed the resort about the tragedy on June 5, 2024, and sought cancellation of the wedding arrangements and a refund. He alleged that the resort threatened to forfeit the entire amount, questioning why the family had booked the property if it was not financially capable of proceeding with the wedding.The complaint further alleged that when Bansal’s father contacted the resort on July 11 to discuss cancellation and refund, a person identifying himself as its vice-president, Vichin Sehgal, misbehaved with him and threatened that he could face trouble from Jaipur Police if he visited the city.Advocate Sudesh K Kataria, appearing for Bansal, placed the complainant’s affidavit, bank statements, contract documents and newspaper reports relating to the factory fire before the commission.The resort, however, did not appear before the commission despite being served notice and was proceeded against ex parte on Aug 20, 2025. Consequently, there was no representation or evidence on its behalf to counter the allegations.The commission observed that there was nothing on record to disbelieve the complainant’s evidence. It also noted that the resort’s absence meant the evidence produced by Bansal remained unrebutted.Holding the resort guilty of deficiency in service, the commission allowed the complaint and ordered the refund with interest and compensation.The commission further warned that failure to comply with the order could lead to execution proceedings under Section 71(1) of the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, and prosecution under Section 72, which provides for imprisonment of one month to three years, a fine of Rs 25,000 to Rs 1 lakh, or both.You Can Also Check: Gold Rate in Gurgaon | Silver Rate in Gurgaon | Bank Holidays in Gurgaon | Public Holidays in Gurgaon | Gurgaon AQI | Weather in Gurgaon | Petrol Price in Gurgaon | Diesel Price in Gurgaon | CNG Price in Gurgaon | LPG Price in GurgaonStay updated with the latest Gurgaon news. articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Thursday accused the ruling Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab of favouritism and irregularities in the Punjab
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Thursday accused the ruling Aam Aadmi Party government in Punjab of favouritism and irregularities in the Punjab Public Service Commission (PPSC) recruitment process. The BJP alleged that several candidates shortlisted for government jobs had links to the Kejriwal-led party and its leaders.Addressing a presser in Delhi, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi questioned the selection of candidates, with the results announced on November 4."There are four categories," Trivedi said, alleging that some shortlisted candidates were related to political leaders and ministers, while others had family connections with officials considered close to the state government.He elaborated on 'four categories' saying, "one consists of people connected to the families of leaders and ministers; the second consists of people connected to the families of officials considered very close to this so-called staunchly honest government; and the third consists of people connected to the families of those facing corruption charges. The fourth category consists of people who have offered some floral tributes to the Aam Aadmi Party, directly or indirectly."Raising questions over the examination pattern, BJP leader said reports that 24% of candidates from a single centre had cleared the examination were suspicious."This in itself raises suspicion," he said, adding that the selection of candidates in different rooms at four examination centres also raised doubts about the process.The allegations come days after several candidates who appeared for the Punjab Civil Services (PCS) and Allied Services examination approached the Punjab and Haryana high court, alleging large-scale irregularities in the selection process.The petitioners have sought a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) probe into the recruitment process, raising questions over the conduct of the examination and the selection of candidates.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: 'Chaos if major powers clash': Xi's warning at trilateral with Trump, Putin - who said what
articles.summary: US President Donald Trump on Thursday met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral summit in Shenzhen on the
articles.body: US President Donald Trump on Thursday met Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin for a trilateral summit in Shenzhen on the sidelines of the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) Summit, describing the meeting as a historic occasion.“We are really making history,” Trump said. “The United States, Russia and China are uniquely positioned to discuss how to reduce the number of nuclear weapons on Earth and also to lessen the risk of those weapons being used.”Trump: Talks on nuclear weapons and 'all problems'Opening the trilateral meeting, Trump said the three leaders would discuss “all problems that are being discussed in the world”. He said the United States, Russia and China were “uniquely positioned” to discuss reducing nuclear weapons and limiting the risk of their use, adding that all three countries had special responsibilities.Trump also stressed the importance of engaging with leaders despite differences, saying that past leaders had too often avoided talks with their counterparts over disagreements."No peace ever forged by declining opportunities," the US president said.Xi: Harmony among major powers 'is a must'Xi described the meeting with Trump and Putin as being of “groundbreaking significance”. According to Chinese state media, he said healthy interactions between major countries were essential.“Healthy interactions between major countries is not optional, is a must,” Xi said.He said the three countries should jointly safeguard global peace and stability and work together to address global challenges. He also warned that the world would be in chaos if major countries fought each other, adding that the world was peaceful when major powers were in harmony."World will be in chaos if major countries fight," he said.Xi further called on the three leaders to learn from history, underlining their shared responsibility in maintaining global peace and stability."Nuclear war cannot be won and must not be fought, every effort must be made to prevent it," Xi added.Xi Jinping said that the United States should do the “right thing” on Taiwan to avoid major setbacks in Sino-American relations, according to the Chinese state news agency Xinhua.Xi added that nuclear weapons should be comprehensively banned and completely dismantled, with the ultimate aim of creating a world free of nuclear weapons.Also check: 'He is my friend': Trump, Putin hold talks ahead of trilateral meeting with Xi on APEC sidelinesPutin: Constructive cooperation can strengthen stabilityPutin said Russia, China and the United States could strengthen global stability through constructive cooperation.Speaking through a translator, he said the three countries had a joint responsibility to maintain peace and security. He also said the leaders should discuss global and regional issues, including energy security.Trump-Xi bilateral talks focus on Hormuz shipping, farm purchasesBefore the trilateral meeting, Trump held a separate bilateral meeting with Xi, marking their third substantial meeting this year. The talks lasted roughly an hour, after which the two leaders and their delegations had lunch.Trump praised his relationship with Xi and highlighted their shared interest in ensuring the continued shipment of oil through the Strait of Hormuz, which has become a key site of attacks during the Iran war.He also indicated that he would press the Chinese leader to increase purchases of American agricultural products.“I’ll be asking you to do some more for our farmers,” Trump said.Xi described relations between the United States and China as “generally stable and improved” during Trump's presidency.“The efforts you have made are there for all to see and will go down in history,” Xi said.Trump holds separate meeting with PutinTrump also held a separate meeting with Putin on the sidelines of the APEC Summit. It was the first time the two leaders had held talks since their discussions in Alaska last year failed to broker a deal to ease Russia's war in Ukraine.After joining Putin for the bilateral meeting, Trump described the Russian president as “my friend” and said, “Wonderful things can come out of this — or at least start.”The two leaders shook hands before their meeting, with Trump adding, “We’ve had a great relationship for many years.”The meeting lasted roughly 40 minutes.You use AI every day. articles.title: Forty years after California's Morongo tribe began sharing Thanksgiving food despite having little to spare, volunteers distributed 15,000 turkeys to 136 groups, taking their reported impact to nearly 4.8 million meals
articles.summary: Forty years after California’s Morongo Band of Mission Indians began sharing Thanksgiving food despite having little to spare, volunteers distributed
articles.body: Forty years after California’s Morongo Band of Mission Indians began sharing Thanksgiving food despite having little to spare, volunteers distributed 15,000 turkeys to 136 groups this week, bringing the tribe’s reported impact to nearly 4.8 million meals. The annual giveaway, now in its 40th year, was reported by KESQ and NBC Palm Springs as a major regional effort to support families, seniors, and people experiencing homelessness during the holidays.The turkeys were distributed from the Morongo Community Center in Banning on November 16 and 17. They will help partner organisations prepare more than 300,000 Thanksgiving meals across the Inland Empire and neighbouring communities.A tradition that began smallThe Morongo Band of Mission Indians started the Thanksgiving turkey giveaway in 1987, when the tribe had limited resources but believed that no one should go hungry during the holidays. Tribal Chairman Charles Martin said that belief has not changed.What began as a modest effort has grown into a large scale annual programme. Over four decades, the tribe says it has distributed nearly 245,000 turkeys and helped provide millions of holiday meals to people in need.This year’s 15,000 turkeys bring the reported total to nearly 4.8 million meals. The number reflects the cumulative impact of decades of giving, not just the current holiday season.How the 2026 giveaway workedTribal members and volunteers gathered at the Morongo Community Center to sort and ship frozen turkeys to 136 organisations. The recipients include nonprofits, churches, and food pantries that will use the birds to prepare meals for their communities.The organisations receiving turkeys are based in Banning, Beaumont, Indio, Los Angeles, Mecca, Moreno Valley, Riverside, San Bernardino, and Temecula. Each group will use its allocation to prepare and serve meals to people who may otherwise go without a Thanksgiving dinner.The tribe begins accepting applications for turkey donations at the beginning of every year. Applications for the 2027 outreach programme are already available through the Morongo Nation website.Who is receiving helpThe Coachella Valley Rescue Mission in Indio received 300 turkeys. Executive Director Amanda Galindo said the donation will help hundreds of men, women, and children who have nowhere else to go enjoy a Thanksgiving meal.The Galilee Center in Mecca also received 300 turkeys. The organisation will use them to support farmworkers, low income families, and seniors as it prepares for its own Thanksgiving food giveaway.Other recipients include Banning based Missionary Baptist Church, which received 100 turkeys, and the Janet Goeske Foundation in Riverside, which received 200. Both organisations plan to use the donations to prepare meals for families and seniors in need.Why the programme mattersFor many recipients, the turkeys are more than food. They represent a chance to share a holiday meal with family, friends, or a community that may otherwise feel distant during the holidays.Caryn Chambers, executive board trustee at Missionary Baptist Church, said, as per the reports, that Morongo’s generosity is a blessing for Banning. She noted that the turkeys will help people enjoy a Thanksgiving dinner they might not have had otherwise.Danielle Stevens, executive director of the Janet Goeske Foundation, said that the holidays can be lonely for many seniors. She explained that a hot meal shared with friends can go a long way, and that Morongo helps make that happen.A legacy of givingThe 40 year milestone gives the programme a sense of continuity. It shows how a small act of generosity can grow into a lasting tradition that reaches thousands of people each year.The tribe’s approach has remained consistent. Rather than changing the mission, it has expanded the scale, adding more partners and more turkeys while keeping the focus on holiday meals.As the 2026 giveaway concludes, the programme is already looking ahead. Applications for 2027 are open, and the tribe says it will continue its effort to make sure more families have a meal to share during the holidays.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. articles.title: As cyberattack hits European Commission, FBI's AI tool warning in focus
articles.summary: A major cyberattack has hit the European Commission, potentially exposing large amounts of personal data, locking staff out of critical human resources
articles.body: A major cyberattack has hit the European Commission, potentially exposing large amounts of personal data, locking staff out of critical human resources systems for more than 10 days, a report has said, adding that the incident has also forced top officials to address the crisis during their weekly meeting on Wednesday (November 18). While the Commission believes it has contained most of the breach, investigators are still working to determine the full scope of the damage.“The systems may be coming back online. The answers are taking a little longer,” said an EU official, speaking on condition of anonymity due to the sensitivity of the matter, as per a report in Politico.How hackers targeted the Commission with an AI toolEarlier this month, CERT-EU, the cybersecurity watchdog for EU institutions, discovered that international hackers were using ARTEX, a publicly available AI-powered tool built to spot weaknesses in IT systems. The EU official said: “Some actors misuse such tools and have targeted the Commission.”In response, the Commission temporarily pulled several applications offline as a precaution, though access to most of them has since been restored. Commission spokesperson Thomas Regnier confirmed that “individual systems were targeted” in a detected cyber campaign and noted that affected parties have been notified in line with standard practice.However, investigators still do not know whether staff data was stolen or how widespread any leak might be. According to the anonymous EU official, this lingering uncertainty is the reason employees have received limited updates so far.The report comes soon after the Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) warned in a FLASH advisory that hackers are using ARTEX, an open-source, large language model (LLM)-driven autonomous penetration testing framework, to automate multiple stages of cyber intrusions. The agency also said hackers have used the tool since at least August to target organisations across financial services, government, technology, defense, semiconductors, energy, healthcare, manufacturing, telecommunications and legal sectors.Over 10 days of workplace disruptionThe cyber incident has caused major day-to-day headaches for Commission employees for more than a week and a half, leaving staff unable to enter salary and leave details:HR and medical platforms: Sysper, which is the Commission's internal HR hub for payslips, leave requests and timesheets, and MyPMO, its medical reimbursement system, were brought back online earlier this week, though Sysper suffered another brief crash.Translation services: Translation tools were also disrupted this week, prompting one frustrated official to admit to “swearing a lot”, Politico reported.Crisis response reaches the highest levelsThe severity of the breach prompted action from the Commission's top leadership. According to a leaked internal email viewed by Playbook (Politico), the Corporate Management Board (the institution's highest internal crisis-management group) held an urgent meeting earlier this month to address the “ongoing cyber incidents.”At the same time, the digital services department rolled out stricter security checks, and Tech Commissioner Henna Virkkunen updated fellow officials on the immediate response during Wednesday's College of Commissioners meeting, two officials confirmed.Your child uses AI every day. articles.title: Denmark buckles under Trump, approves US military expansion deal in Greenland
articles.summary: Denmark's parliament on Thursday voted in favour of a security agreement with the United States, clearing the final parliamentary hurdle for a deal that
articles.body: Denmark's parliament on Thursday voted in favour of a security agreement with the United States, clearing the final parliamentary hurdle for a deal that will expand Washington's military presence in Greenland.The approval comes months after US President Donald Trump repeatedly threatened to take control of the strategically important Arctic island, triggering tensions between Washington and its Nato allies.According to the agreement, the US will gain expanded military access to Greenland, including the right to modernise existing defence facilities and establish additional military infrastructure on the island.The deal also provides a framework for strengthening American missile defence capabilities in the Arctic, including support for Trump's proposed Golden Dome system.The agreement builds on the 1951 US-Denmark defence pact and is aimed at strengthening security cooperation in the Arctic. It also seeks to limit the military and strategic presence of countries outside Nato in Greenland, amid growing US concerns over Russia and China's ambitions in the region.Reuters reported that the agreement was negotiated after months of diplomatic tensions over Trump's ambition to bring Greenland under US control. While Washington has sought a greater military and strategic role on the island, Denmark has maintained that Greenland's sovereignty is non-negotiable. The agreement provides a way to expand US military access without changing Greenland's political status.Why Greenland is strategically important to the USGreenland's strategic importance to the US stems primarily from its geographical location between North America, Europe and the Arctic.The island is home to the US-operated Pituffik Space Base, which plays a key role in missile warning, missile defence and space surveillance. Its location allows Washington to monitor potential missile threats approaching North America and track military activity across the Arctic.Greenland also lies along the Greenland-Iceland-UK (GIUK) gap, a strategically important maritime corridor used to monitor Russian submarines and naval movements between the Arctic and the North Atlantic.The growing military and economic competition between the US, Russia and China has further increased the island's importance.Russia has expanded its military infrastructure in the Arctic, while China has sought a greater economic and strategic presence in the region. Melting Arctic ice is also opening the possibility of new shipping routes, creating opportunities for trade and access to natural resources.Washington sees Greenland as a critical location to strengthen its position in the region and counter the growing influence of its rivals.Greenland's mineral wealth is another major factor behind US interest. The island has significant deposits of rare earth elements and other critical minerals used in fighter jets, missile systems, electronics and advanced technologies.Access to these resources could help Washington diversify its supply chains and reduce dependence on China, which dominates much of the global rare earth processing industry. articles.title: Alpha, performative, toxic: Navigating the social media labels
articles.summary: Written By: Harsh Kashiv From the “alpha male” who commands attention to the “performative male” whose emotional expression is questioned, social media
articles.body: Written By: Harsh Kashiv From the “alpha male” who commands attention to the “performative male” whose emotional expression is questioned, social media has created new labels through which men are judged. Caught between traditional expectations of toughness and newer demands for emotional sensitivity, men are navigating competing ideas of what it means to be masculine. Psychologists and cultural observers say these labels leave little room for individual differences. They point out that confidence need not translate into dominance, vulnerability is not weakness, and a man’s identity does not depend on external approval.‘Men don’t need to hide their emotions’Clinical psychologist Anshul Goel says traditional ideas of masculinity have discouraged men from expressing emotions, often treating crying and vulnerability as signs of weakness. “Traditionally, men have been tailored to be tough, macho and often required not to express their emotions or cry because that makes them a ‘woman’. Men don’t need to hide away their emotions, their feelings and their being,” he says. Referring to Carl Jung’s concept of the anima, Goel says men need not suppress qualities traditionally associated with femininity. “Men are more than capable of expressing themselves... Men don’t require constant validation and approval to be manly enough. They don’t require permission to express how they feel, to be the way they want to be,” he adds.‘Masculinity comes in new formats and vocabularies’Shamika Dixit, a professor of media and culture studies, says patriarchal expectations have also harmed men — a dimension that often receives less attention in conversations about gender. “With the rise of hypermasculine cultures, social media or internet cultures at the broadest level have been pushing men into echo chambers of traditional expectations of masculinity. We see those expectations coming to us in newer formats, new vocabulary and new audiences. Sometimes under the hood of ‘joke’, sometimes under the name of ‘cuteness’ and now through the AI slop we see this re-emergence, which is hard to avoid and difficult to label as it becomes a part of hegemony,” she says, adding, “The alpha male and the performative male might appear to occupy opposite ends of the masculine spectrum, but both can become carefully curated identities performed for an audience.”‘When real human beings fall short of polarised ideals, they feel trapped and inadequate’The pressure to conform to competing ideals can leave men feeling inadequate, says theatre director and playwright Ankit Gor. While one image glorifies aggression and emotional restraint, another expects men to be ambitious yet emotionally sensitive. “Society expects men to tick every single box: be unyielding and driven, yet entirely emotionally articulate and sensitive… When real human beings fall short of these polarised ideals, they feel trapped and inadequate,” he says. Gor says social media has further blurred the line between authentic behaviour and performance, with everyday actions quickly labelled. “Sensitive men who genuinely want to navigate their emotions struggle the most because whatever they do triggers a label. If they express feelings, they’re judged; if they bottle them up, they’re condemned as toxic. … Human emotion isn’t clean-cut,” he adds. ‘Men must prioritise their own health’Senior psychologist Prashant Bhimani says repeated labels and online trolling can shape how individuals perceive themselves. “When someone is labelled or tagged, the primary problem arises when they either begin to strongly internalise those negative beliefs or fall into deep internal conflict resisting them. Over time, these tags function as psychological conditioning,” he says. He adds that an internal locus of control can help people reject inaccurate labels, while absorbing external praise or criticism may lead to superiority or inferiority complexes. Bhimani says online reactions have made it harder to assess opinions before accepting them. “Establishing a solid identity requires three pillars: self-confidence, willpower and self-esteem,” he says, adding that men should express their emotions, care for their physical health and seek professional help when needed. “Men must actively free themselves from reductive stereotypes,” he adds.You use AI every day. articles.title: ‘Face-to-face contest’: Yogi challenges Akhilesh to contest UP polls from Ayodhya
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday challenged Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to contest elections against him from
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh chief minister Yogi Adityanath on Thursday challenged Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav to contest elections against him from Ayodhya, saying he would also file his nomination from the constituency if Yadav accepted the challenge.“If you file your nomination from there, I will also file my nomination. Let there be a direct, face-to-face contest,” Adityanath said while addressing a public rally.He accused Yadav of lacking the courage to contest elections head-on, alleging that a weak person always strikes from behind.“He lacks the courage to fight head-on because a weak person always strikes from behind,” he said.Yogi Adityanath targets SP over boy's death during Akhilesh Yadav's roadshowAdityanath also targeted the Samajwadi Party over the death of a 13-year-old boy during Yadav's roadshow in Gorakhpur on Wednesday, describing the party as synonymous with hooliganism, anarchy, riots and lawlessness. He vowed strict action against those responsible for the incident.Addressing a programme in Campierganj in Gorakhpur district, the chief minister referred to the death of Aryavardhan, son of local BJP leader Onkar Singh, who was allegedly run over by an excavator during the roadshow.“What was the fault of that innocent boy, barely 13 years old?” he asked, alleging that the Samajwadi Party had made the child a victim of its roadshow.Adityanath said the boy, who was studying at a reputed school and living with his family, had been killed in a "brutal" manner. He also criticised those he accused of supporting mafia elements and hooliganism for not even expressing condolences over the death."I express my condolences over the death of this innocent boy. I am also going to meet his family this evening and express my sympathy," he said.The chief minister accused the SP of having links with mafia elements and betraying and exploiting the public. He said his government had curbed hooliganism and was preparing to take further action against those indulging in such activities."If anyone tries to indulge in mafiagiri, it will not take long to reduce that mafia to dust. The Samajwadi Party is synonymous with hooliganism, anarchy, riots, and curfews. Every mafia is their ally, and they have always betrayed the public. Just as a dog's tail can never be straightened, these goons and mafias cannot be reformed unless they are straightened out with the force of the law, and that is precisely what our government is doing. We have curbed their hooliganism, and we are preparing to tighten the noose on them once again,” he said.Adityanath said he had instructed the administration to identify those who had created disturbances on the roads and ensure they were punished.He also said that roads in Uttar Pradesh had been built to facilitate the movement of the public and not for workers of the Samajwadi Party and Congress to create disorder."Good roads have not been built so that goons of the SP and Congress come and create disorder. If anyone tries to display mafia behaviour again, there will be no delay in crushing that mafia," he said.The chief minister further warned those allegedly attempting to create disorder and forcibly secure public support, saying the people of Uttar Pradesh had repeatedly rejected them and would do so again in the 2027 elections.He also said women and girls were able to move freely because they trusted the BJP government under Prime Minister Narendra Modi to ensure their safety.Warning against encroachment on the land of the poor and threats to women's safety, Adityanath said those responsible would face "either jail or hell", with no third option.The boy's death triggered protests by his family members and BJP workers in Gorakhpur on Wednesday. Protesters blocked the Gorakhpur-Deoria road, demanding action against the excavator driver and those who had arranged the machine for the roadshow.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Rahul Gandhi calls Indian democracy 'sacred'; BJP launches attack after hearing 'sick'
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday launched a broadside against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his remarks at an event in Chicago.
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday launched a broadside against Lok Sabha leader of opposition Rahul Gandhi over his remarks at an event in Chicago. BJP leaders claimed that Rahul Gandhi called Indian democracy "sick". The video put out by news agencies, however, showed that he had actually described the democracy as "sacred".In a social media post on X, BJP national spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari shared a clip of Rahul's address and termed him "leader of anti-India propaganda.""Rahul Gandhi called Indian Democracy 'sick' from foreign soil! Congress calls Indian democracy 'sick'. Rahul Gandhi has yet again proven he loves Parivar, & hates Democracy!" Bhandari said."Every time Rahul proves he is against Indian state, People of India & India's Democratic Fabric! Rahul Gandhi is Leader of Anti India Propaganda!" he added.Several BJP leaders also followed Bhandari in attacking Rahul, saying that the Congress leader was "moving towards senile mental dementia.""Rahul Gandhi himself is sick; he has been unwell for 10 years. He has developed an illness called obsessive-compulsive neurosis for the past 10 years, and now he is gradually moving towards senile mental dementia," BJP spokesperson Ajay Alok said."He has become incoherent. Look at him - he has no sense of place, time, or object. He thinks one thing in his mind, and something else comes out of his mouth. What was he even trying to say? Saying about his own mother that at every mile, Mummy used to sit in Papa's lap. Does Indian society speak like that or think like that? So, he is gradually losing his balance," he added.What Rahul actually saidDuring an interaction with students at the University of Chicago in the US, Rahul Gandhi was asked why the opposition does not boycott elections if it believes they were being rigged.The Congress leader said Indian democracy was "sacred" to him and that he would need overwhelming evidence to even claim that it was under threat."Indian democracy is sacred. For me to even say that there is a problem in Indian democracy is difficult without 100, 200, 300 per cent proof," Rahul said."But what happens to all the opposition workers if we tell them, 'Okay, don't participate in the election?' If we say that we are not going to contest elections, we end Indian democracy that minute. And we don't want to end the structure of Indian democracy," he said.Rahul said the opposition's strategy was to highlight alleged electoral irregularities and continue contesting elections until people realise what he claimed was the dismantling of the system."So, our strategy is to expose what is going on and take the beating until the people of India realise that the system has been fully demolished," he added.BJP has repeatedly criticised Rahul Gandhi over his remarks during foreign visits, accusing him of maligning India and its democratic institutions.The latest controversy comes after Rahul raised allegations of "vote chori" during an earlier interaction at Columbia University, prompting BJP leaders to accuse him of insulting India and its democracy.Rahul was on a two-day visit to the US during which he interacted with students at Columbia University in New York on Tuesday and the University of Chicago on Wednesday.Get the latest India News and Live updates. articles.title: Turkey lands, launches combat drones from highways: A lesson for Pakistan, a worry for India
articles.summary: Turkey has in an exercise operated its Akinci and TB2 drones from a highway.
articles.body: Turkey has in an exercise operated its Akinci and TB2 drones from a highway. This exercise highlights how roads can be used as alternative operating surfaces for military aircraft when conventional runways are unavailable in times of both a conflict or during a calamity. The development is relevant to India as Pakistan operates both these types of drones. Recently during Operation Sindoor, India had smashed many Pakistani air bases, which in times of conflict would force Islamabad to use of road infrastructure to improve the dispersal and survivability of its air assets.Turkey has demonstrated a new dimension of military operations by successfully landing and taking off combat drones from a highway during an emergency exercise. Three unmanned aircraft — an Akinci and two Bayraktar TB2 drones — converged on the Manisa-Balikesir Highway after taking off from separate bases at Kesan, Corlu and Izmir. The exercise, conducted by defence company Baykar in coordination with Turkey's defence ministry and highways authorities, was designed to demonstrate that unmanned combat aircraft could continue operating when conventional runways were unavailable. Baykar plans to extend the concept to other indigenous platforms, including the Kizilelma unmanned fighter and Bayraktar TB3.Such exercises are becoming increasingly important as air forces prepare for the possibility of conventional airbases being damaged by missiles, drones or precision strikes during a conflict. Dispersing aircraft across alternative operating locations can reduce dependence on a handful of major airfields and provide greater flexibility in sustaining operations. Highway-based operations, however, require more than a suitable stretch of road. They involve coordination with civilian authorities, traffic closures, security arrangements and ground support. Turkey's exercise also illustrates how unmanned aircraft, which generally have different runway requirements from conventional fighters, can add another dimension to this concept.Pakistan has practised highway operations for several years, the Pakistan Air Force demonstrated the use of the Islamabad-Lahore M-2 Motorway during Exercise High Mark in April 2010, when Mirage III and F-7PG fighters landed, were refuelled and rearmed before taking off. Similar operations were conducted in March 2019 at multiple, publicly unidentified highway locations and again on the M-2 in October 2020. The M-1 Islamabad-Peshawar Motorway also has a documented four-kilometre section designed as an emergency airstrip.In a conflict with India, such facilities could give the PAF alternative locations to recover aircraft and potentially resume sorties if conventional airbases were temporarily unavailable. They could complicate efforts to restrict operations to established airfields and improve dispersal. However, highway landings alone cannot replace a fully equipped airbase, particularly for sustained combat operations requiring maintenance, weapons handling and secure logistics.India has developed a similar capability. Its first Emergency Landing Facility on a national highway was inaugurated on the Satta-Gandhav stretch of NH-925A near Barmer, Rajasthan, in September 2021. The IAF has also practised operations on the Yamuna and Agra-Lucknow expressways. In April 2026, it activated the Purvanchal Expressway facility in Sultanpur for day and night operations involving Sukhoi-30MKI, Mirage-2000, Jaguar, C-295 and AN-32 aircraft. India is thus expanding a network of alternative landing facilities along strategic road corridors.
